title: [finding] the `spec-property-retirement` playbook prescribes a `major` changeset that a live per-PR gate refuses — copy the checklist line verbatim and the PR reddens
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` seat 3 (`session_01HnRAeVTLJevtQ5iCPX6JSm`), ⏱️ 2026-09-20T13:20Z. ⛔ Not triaged, ⛔ no `domain:*`, ⛔ no priority. Lands on `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md` — governed `.claude/**` (Tier S) ⇒ **`domain:skills`** by the domain table. Surfaced by the `os-dev` executing #18623; ⛔ that dev correctly did not file it itself.

## The contradiction, both halves read on `origin/main` this act

| side | text |
|:--|:--|
| the playbook, `.claude/skills/spec-property-retirement/SKILL.md:291` | `- [ ] **Changeset** —— \`@objectstack/spec\` 用 \`major\`。AGENTS.md:breaking` |
| the gate, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:5-6` (its own header) | 「**LAUNCH-WINDOW GUARD** — a PR may not introduce a changeset that declares a \`major\` bump.」 |

The gate is **live per-PR**, wired into `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` as the `Check Changeset` job.

⇒ An agent that follows the retirement playbook's own checklist line **writes a changeset the gate rejects**, and the PR goes red for doing exactly what the instructions said.

## Why class (a) and not a doc nit

This is the 「示例照抄即失败」 shape the triage rules name as the dividing line for (a): the playbook is a **checklist an agent executes verbatim**, not prose it interprets. The failure is reproducible by construction — write the changeset the line prescribes, open a PR, `Check Changeset` refuses it.

⚠️ It also costs more than a red: an agent that hits it must then decide whether the **playbook** or the **gate** is authoritative, mid-round, on a card that is usually already a delicate public-surface deletion.

## ⭐ Measured consequence, so the fix is not guessed

On **#18623** this contradiction was live: its ruling (`5725503716`, maintainer 「同意」) specifies changeset **`minor`**, while the playbook says `major`. ⇒ the ruling's `minor` is both binding **and** the only gate-compatible level, so that card needed no stop — but the next retirement without an explicit level in its ruling has nothing to break the tie.

## Fix

One line in the playbook: the retirement changeset is **`minor`** (with the BREAKING banner carrying the semantics), ⛔ not `major`, while the launch-window guard stands. Ideally with a pointer to the gate so the next reader sees why.

⛔ This seat did not edit `.claude/**` — governed surface, skills lane, and this seat is not that lane.

## Dedupe words

`spec-property-retirement changeset major` · `check-changeset-no-major playbook` · `SKILL.md major bump` · `launch-window guard refuses major` · `retirement playbook stale changeset level`
